decisions.context: Weekly forecasting needs repeatable preparation, training, evaluation, and release steps. A three-person team benefits from reducing manual coordination.
decisions.rationale: Choose a repeatable pipeline to support the weekly run and get model changes through preparation, evaluation, and deployment with less manual coordination. Practitioners describe connected pipeline stages in “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning.”
consequences: Pipeline stages and dependencies need maintenance.
Workflow orchestration becomes a production dependency.

decisions.decision: Track the full ML lifecycle for reproducibility
decisions.context: Reproducing a past week requires retaining the data and training context behind each forecast. Artifact-only versioning does not cover the complete lifecycle.
decisions.rationale: Choose lifecycle-wide tracking so past forecasts can be tied to dataset versions, pipeline definitions, dependencies, and training runs. “MLOps: What It Is, Why it Matters, and How To Implement It (from a Data Scientist Perspective)” describes these practices together.
consequences: Dataset snapshots and run metadata must be retained.
Reproducibility depends on capturing pipeline and dependency changes.

decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly without disrupting the weekly run. Releases need repeatable validation and a controlled path into production.
decisions.rationale: Choose repository-triggered builds and tests with staged promotion to speed delivery while providing checkpoints before production. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” describes commit-triggered releases across delivery stages.
consequences: Release checks must finish before promotion.
Staging environments and promotion rules require ownership.

decisions.context: Model changes must not break forecasts already used by the weekly run. Candidate quality needs assessment before a release reaches production.
decisions.rationale: Choose held-out offline evaluation as a pre-release quality gate, with the pipeline running it consistently before model promotion. “MLOps Principles” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” describe offline evaluation in the delivery workflow.
consequences: Evaluation data and criteria need versioning.

decisions.decision: Monitor input and feature drift in production
decisions.context: Weekly forecasts can become unreliable as retail inputs change. The brief gives no requirement for fully automatic retraining, so drift monitoring provides visibility without assuming retraining policy.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
cons: Drift may not mean quality loss

decisions.rationale: Choose drift monitoring to surface changes in schemas and feature distributions that could affect weekly forecasts. “Machine Learning Monitoring: What It Is, and What We Are Missing” and “MLOps Principles” describe monitoring these changes.
consequences: Monitoring signals need review and response ownership.
Drift alerts alone do not establish forecast degradation.

uncovered: Data ingestion mechanism and source-system integration; the checked design point indicates workflow coordination requires this decision.
